Unusual case of jerking stiff person syndrome
N. Chaudhary, S. Jaiswal, J.M.K. Murthy (Hyderabad, India)
Objective: To study a case of stiff person syndrome with jerking
and autonomic dysfunction with reference to Clinical, Neurophysio-
logical characteristics.
Background: A 56 yr male admitted with history of recurrent
episodes of stiffness involving axial and appendicular musculature
predominatly involving quadriceps.
These episodes are associated with profuse sweating, transient
dilatation of pupils and tachycardia.
There were recurrent jerking predominantly involving axial Mus-
culature.
On examination there was associated rigidity also.
This jerking used to precipitate spontaneously or with external
stimulus as light, sound or touch.
Methods: We used clinical history, neurophysiological studies
(EMG, EEG), and neuroimaging to characterise syndrome.
Results: EMG showed continuous muscle ﬁbre activity in para-
spinal muscles.
Anti GAD Antibody and Anti NMDA receptor antibody were
negative.
MRI brain and spine were normal.
He was treated with phenytoin and diazepam and his symptoms
resolved.
Conclusions: This patient had a rare form of reﬂex & spontane-
ous myoclonus with associated muscular rigidity similar to that seen
in the stiffman syndrome with rigidity. These syndromes represent a
clinical spectrum of stiffperson syndrome and the mechanism of the
rigidity, spasms, and in this case myoclonus, may localize in the
brainstem or the spinal cord.
